items.title: Kenya and Switzerland deepen bilateral climate partnership at COP 31
items.description: Kenya and Switzerland deepen bilateral climate partnership at COP 31 Kenya News Agency Kenya and Switzerland authorise first Article 6.2 carbon programme for 226,000 Roam electric motorcycles THE PACK – Electric motorcycle news Cabinet Secretary (CS) for Environment, Climate Change and Forestry, Dr. Deborah Barasa (Right) poses for a photo with the landmark Kenya–Switzerland Article 6 Implementing Agreement during high-level bilateral engagements at the Swiss Delegation Offi Facebook Swiss approve 1st project under Kenyan Art. 6 deal for 1.7m ITMOs Quantum Commodity Intelligence
content: Environment, Climate Change and Forestry Cabinet Secretary, Dr. Deborah Barasa has reaffirmed Kenya’s commitment to operationalizing the landmark Kenya–Switzerland Article 6 Implementing Agreement during high-level bilateral engagements at the Swiss Delegation Office on the sidelines of COP 31.

Following the Agreement’s signing in Bern in May 2025 and its entry into force in June 2026, both nations are moving decisively from policy to implementation to unlock high-integrity carbon markets that drive climate action and economic growth.

This strategic partnership is projected to deliver 5 million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent in mitigation outcomes while mobilizing USD 520 million in direct investments, generating USD 200 million in carbon revenues alongside USD 21.2 million in Designated National Authority (DNA) fees, and creating approximately 115,000 green jobs.
Further, momentum on the ground is already building, with eight projects registered across electric mobility, biogas, solar water pumping, and clean cooking.

Notably, four of these initiatives have already received Letters of Approval from Kenya’s DNA, including the recent issuance of a revised Letter of Approval for Roam Electric in October 2026, underscoring the Government’s commitment to facilitating implementation within its existing legal framework.

During the engagements, Dr. Barasa emphasized regulatory predictability and investor confidence, pointing to the Government’s formal communication to Switzerland on 6 th , November 2026 that confirmed Kenya’s authorization pathway.

“Under the Climate Change Act (Cap. 387A) and the Carbon Markets Regulations, 2024, Kenya remains committed to authorizing eligible projects, applying corresponding adjustments, and recognizing the international transfer and use of verified Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs),” the CS reaffirmed.

Furthermore, she noted that the mitigation volumes for activities with Letters of Approval have already been factored into Kenya’s carbon budget under the Kenya Guide for Strategic Engagement in Carbon Markets (2026).

While both countries issue their own independent authorizations under their respective domestic laws, Kenya has proposed establishing a Joint Technical Working Group—bringing together representatives from Switzerland, NEMA, the Climate Change Directorate, and the Ministry’s Legal Unit, to swiftly address any emerging technical or regulatory challenges.

Alongside this, Dr. Barasa called for expedited Swiss reviews and authorizations for projects that have already fulfilled Kenya’s domestic regulatory requirements to fast-track financial closure and investment mobilization.

Meanwhile, the Ministry remains steadfast in working closely with Switzerland to champion transparent, high-integrity carbon markets that deliver tangible climate resilience, green investments, and sustainable development for all Kenyans.

content: Residents of Mandera County can now obtain their Certificate of Good Conduct in less than three minutes following the launch of a biometric identification system at the Huduma Centre in Mandera town.

The new system, introduced by the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), is expected to reduce delays previously experienced by applicants, who sometimes waited for several weeks to receive their clearance certificates.
Speaking during the launch, Mandera East DCIO Hassan Yattani said the new technology would bring services closer to residents and improve the efficiency of the clearance process.
“Through this new system, residents can now obtain their Certificates of Good Conduct in less than three minutes, compared to the previous process, which could take more than two weeks,” said Hassan.
The DCI urged residents who require the certificates for employment and other official purposes to visit the Huduma Centre and take advantage of the improved service.
The services in Mandera are part of the Government’s nationwide strategy to decentralize police clearance services and bring them closer to the people.
The service, which was launched today, has already received positive feedback from applicants, with beneficiaries praising the faster processing of certificates and the efficiency of the new system.
Residents who received their certificates during the launch welcomed the new system, saying it would save them time and reduce the challenges associated with the previous application process.
A beneficiary Daud Ali said applicants previously experienced long waiting periods, sometimes extending to several months.

“We are grateful that we have finally received our certificates within just two minutes. Previously, obtaining them was a major challenge, and we appreciate the authorities for bringing this service closer to us,” Daud said.
Another beneficiary also welcomed the improvement, saying he had applied and received his certificate on the same day.
The biometric system is expected to make access to police clearance services faster and more convenient for residents of Mandera County.

items.title: Upgrade of 80-year-old Maai Mahiu escarpment road to four lanes starts in January, says KeNHA
items.description: KeNHA says the four-lane upgrade will ease decades of congestion.
content: A section of the Maai Mahiu - Naivasha escarpment road that is set for expansion to a four lane highway

After decades of pleas and protests, the government is set to expand the 23-kilometre Maai Mahiu escarpment highway, built by Italian prisoners of war in the 1940s, following years of complaints from motorists and members of the public.
The planned upgrade to a four-lane highway is expected to begin in January 2027, according to the Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA).

The expansion is expected to ease transport challenges that have persisted for decades, particularly traffic snarl-ups caused by trucks breaking down on the steep, rocky terrain, which is challenging for motorists to navigate.

President William Ruto said during the State of the Nation address in Parliament last Wednesday that approximately 7,000 kilometres of roads were under construction across the country, as his administration targets tarmacking 28,000 kilometres and dualling 2,500 kilometres of highways.
President William Ruto delivers the State of the Nation address at Parliament Buildings, Nairobi, on November 18, 2026.

Dr Ruto said his administration was prioritising the Kamandura-Maai Mahiu-Naivasha road, which he had also announced three days earlier in Narok would be upgraded to a four-lane highway to ease decades of congestion.

The road was constructed in the early 1940s by Italian prisoners of war, who also built a small church at the foot of the escarpment, on the outskirts of Maai Mahiu trading centre. The church has since become a major tourist attraction.
The highway, a key link between Nairobi, Western Kenya through the Rift Valley and neighbouring East African countries, will be expanded from the current two lanes to four.
In an update following inquiries by the Nation , KeNHA said the project sponsor had proposed to commence construction on the A8 South section in January 2027.

"The commencement schedule for the respective project sections will be implemented in accordance with the applicable project arrangements and approvals," KeNHA stated in a response from its corporate communications department.
On the implementation timelines, the authority said the project sponsor had prepared a construction schedule with defined timelines and committed to working towards achieving them.
"The sponsor is expected to monitor implementation progress and put in place appropriate mitigation measures to address any challenges that may arise and affect the planned schedule," KeNHA stated.
The authority said the detailed road designs were not yet available and would be released once finalised.

"The project design is still under development and reviewed by the Contracting Authority and the Project Sponsor. The available design is at preliminary stages and may change as more refinement is done," KeNHA stated.

Kenya hosted an average of 35,000 to 55,000 Italian prisoners of war in 11 detention camps, with the one in Maai Mahiu designated Camp 352. They were captured by British and imperial forces in Ethiopia, Somalia and Eritrea during World War II.

The smallest catholic church in Africa, measuring 15 by 8 feet, seating 12 worshippers, and without a presiding priest, was constructed by Italian Prisoners of War in 1942, at the foot of the Maai Mahiu escarpment road set for upgrade to a four-lane highway, in this photo taken on November 20, 2026. The Kenya National Highway Authority (KENHA) says the church would not be demolished in the planned upgrade of the road that will commence in January 2027.
Most of the prisoners, who were sailors and soldiers, were forced into manual labour, including the construction of the Maai Mahiu road.

The Italian prisoners also built a Catholic church in 1942, popularly known as the Travellers' Chapel. It is recognised as the smallest church in East Africa and has a history spanning three countries on two continents: Kenya, Britain and France.

The pentagonal architectural structure has four wooden pews that can accommodate 12 worshippers, representing the number of Jesus' disciples as recorded in the Bible. It was built by the prisoners under the supervision of British colonial authorities.
The church operates 24 hours a day and has an open-door policy, allowing motorists to stop for prayers, conduct weddings or simply visit.

Bishop McCarthy of the Catholic Church and the then Governor of the Kenya Colony, Sir Henry Moore, granted permission for its construction following a request by the Italian prisoners, who were Catholic, while the British were Anglicans.
There are concerns among residents and motorists about the fate of the church once construction begins, with calls for the government to ensure it is spared demolition.

"This church has a very deep historical attachment with Kenya's independence with the fact it was built by Italian Prisoners of War and has been a key tourism site for over 80 years. We do not expect the government to demolish it," said Ann Nyakio, the church's caretaker for the past 18 years.

A signage showing the smallest church in Africa, at the foot of Maai Mahiu escarpment road, that Kenya National Highway Authority (KENHA) says would not be demolished with the infrastructure set for upgrade to a four lane highway, in this photo taken on November 20, 2026.

Ms Nyakio said the church had received partial maintenance support from the Italian Embassy in Kenya over the years and attracted thousands of local and foreign tourists. Its demolition, she added, would negatively affect tourism and religion.
However, KeNHA said the design currently under consideration would not interfere with or disrupt the operations of the church facilities.
The highway runs through Nakuru and Kiambu counties, linking the Rift Valley, Mount Kenya and Nairobi regions.
At Maai Mahiu trading centre, the Nairobi-Naivasha highway extends towards Nakuru, Eldoret and Malaba, while a turn-off towards Narok leads to Bomet, Kisii and Sirare.

Thousands of trucks transporting goods to and from Tanzania through the Isebania border, as well as Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo, South Sudan and Rwanda through the Malaba border, use the highway.

Raw and processed agricultural produce from the Port of Mombasa, industries in Nairobi, Kiambu, Machakos and Kajiado counties, and farming regions in the Rift Valley, Western, Mount Kenya and Eastern regions is also transported through the route.

President Ruto has also said the government is seeking to ease transport challenges through the construction of the Suswa-Ngong road, which will disperse traffic heading to Nairobi and other regions, bypassing the congestion-prone Maai Mahiu route.

Another road has been constructed through Maai Mahiu, passing near Kijabe Mission Hospital and connecting to the main Nairobi-Nakuru highway, to ease congestion on the escarpment and provide an alternative route when the main road is blocked.
The planned expansion is also expected to affect curio stalls along the escarpment.

"The planned expansion of the Mai Mahiu-Rironi road is a major infrastructural undertaking that will solve decades of challenges for motorists using saloon vehicles, passenger service vehicles and trucks," Narok Governor Patrick Ntutu said.
The hilly and rocky terrain is expected to make construction particularly demanding, requiring specialised equipment and expertise.
"Design and implementation of the works will require a lot of expertise and equipment, that may lead to temporary closure of the highway to curb possible accidents," roads contractor Paul Kirui said.
Mr Kirui said Chinese engineering experts could be useful given their experience in constructing roads through similarly hilly and rocky terrain.
Trucks frequently break down along the highway, causing traffic snarl-ups that leave motorists with no alternative route and trapped in gridlocks for several hours.
Accidents have also repeatedly occurred along the escarpment, with vehicles plunging over cliffs, making it difficult to retrieve wreckage and sometimes resulting in fatalities.

"I have on occasions been forced to stay on the highway for over six hours due to accidents that have caused traffic jams with the police called in to restore order," said Elijah Mosintet, a Narok resident.
On proposals to install cable cars along the escarpment, KeNHA said discussions on their implementation had not yet taken place.

"The Contracting Authority and the Project Sponsor are currently focused on finalizing and reviewing the road designs. The proposal will be discussed at a subsequent stage, following the finalization of the road designs," the authority stated.

Roads Cabinet Secretary Davis Chirchir said last week that the government planned to introduce cable cars on the Great Rift Valley escarpment in a project expected to attract more tourists and boost economic growth.
The cable cars would offer users a bird's-eye view of the Great Rift Valley around the Mt Longonot area.
Tourism Principal Secretary Julius Bitok said introducing cable cars would be an expensive undertaking requiring private sector participation.
"Cable cars are expensive ventures that will require private investors to be on-boarded to ensure its success. It is a worthy venture that will boost tourism," Prof Bitok said on Tuesday.
He added that there was also a possibility of introducing cable cars along the Kerio Valley escarpment to boost tourism in the North Rift region.

Court orders DCI boss to appear in court over missing Tanzanian activist Twaha Mwaipaya
items.description: The High Court has ordered the Director of Criminal Investigations (DCI) to appear before court on December 3, 2026, to explain the progress of investigations into the disappearance of Tanzanian activist Twaha Mwaipaya.
content: The High Court has ordered the Director of Criminal Investigations (DCI) to appear before court on December 3, 2026, to explain the progress of investigations into the disappearance of Tanzanian activist Twaha Mwaipaya.
Justice Alexander Muteti issued the summons, directing the DCI to provide a detailed update on efforts to trace Mwaipaya, who was allegedly abducted in Ruai, Nairobi, on October 25, 2026.

In his ruling, Justice Muteti observed that the DCI was a competent and necessary witness capable of providing critical information on the investigations, particularly because the Inspector General of Police had informed the court that the matter was being handled by the DCIO Ruai, whose officers fall under the DCI’s command.

The judge expressed concern over the time that had elapsed since Mwaipaya’s disappearance, stressing that the State could not allow investigations into alleged enforced disappearances to continue indefinitely without providing meaningful updates to the court.

The court underscored that the matter raised serious constitutional concerns, including Mwaipaya’s right to life under Article 26 and his right to freedom and security of the person under Article 29 of the Constitution.
The applicants had sought to have both the DCI and the Deputy Inspector General of Police summoned to explain police operations and the steps taken to establish the activist’s whereabouts.
They argued that the appearance of the senior security officials would enhance accountability and help the court establish what the police had done to locate Mwaipaya.

However, the respondents opposed the application, maintaining that the Inspector General had already provided the National Police Service’s position and that the applicants had failed to demonstrate what additional information the two officers would bring before the court.
The Attorney General’s counsel further argued that the application was an attempt to review previous court orders.

In determining the application, Justice Muteti declined to summon the Deputy Inspector General, finding that his testimony was unlikely to provide substantially new information beyond what had already been presented by the Inspector General.
However, the judge ruled that the DCI’s direct involvement in overseeing criminal investigations made his appearance necessary to account for the progress of the probe.

Justice Muteti further emphasised that investigating alleged human rights violations was a constitutional obligation of the State and that police investigations must be conducted seriously, independently and expeditiously.
The court warned against treating investigations into alleged disappearances as mere formalities or leaving the responsibility of pursuing answers entirely to victims and their families.
The DCI is now expected to appear before the court on December 3 and provide a comprehensive account of investigative steps undertaken to establish Mwaipaya.

items.title: Gachagua Announces December Political Direction for Mt. Kenya and Endorses Gelonga Mkunji for Embu Governor

content: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua addressed congregants during a church service at Wonders of God Church in Runyenjes, Embu County, where he outlined a m...

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua addressed congregants during a church service at Wonders of God Church in Runyenjes, Embu County, where he outlined a major political realignment for the Mount Kenya region ahead of the upcoming general election. Gachagua welcomed Runyenjes Member of Parliament Muchangi Karemba back to the regional fold, noting that Karemba had listened to the sentiments of his constituents on the ground and decided to abandon President William Ruto's political camp. Emphasizing that all politics is local, Gachagua praised Karemba, alongside lawmakers Kagombe and Gathoni Wamuchomba (referred to as Mkami), for resonating with the desires of their electorate rather than remaining tied to political arrangements in Nairobi.
"What a clever leader does, you listen to your people and these are your people. All politics is local hapa mlimani," Gachagua stated.

Gachagua announced that the Mount Kenya region will make its definitive political decisions for the next election during the upcoming Christmas festivities, between December 23 and Boxing Day on December 26. He explained that residents working in Nairobi and elsewhere will travel home to consult with their families and agree on preferred candidates for every elective seat, from the presidency down to Members of County Assemblies. Ahead of the holiday break, Gachagua pledged to issue a clear political direction on December 22 or 23, asking residents to deliberate on his guidance over Christmas and report back with any proposed adjustments by December 27 or 28.
"So promise before we break for Christmas, we shall give political direction for this region so that tukikula Christmas tukubaliane vizuri," he said.

Reflecting on past political alliances, Gachagua used the metaphor of hiring a vehicle for a wedding only to be abandoned along the way to describe the region's fallout with President Ruto. He declared that the Mount Kenya electorate has resolved never again to rely on another leader's political vehicle, announcing that they now have their own green-colored party, the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), which he described as the color of restoration and prosperity. Dismissing rival political outfits—including Ruto's yellow party and smaller parties being introduced in Runyenjes and Manyatta to confuse voters—Gachagua insisted that the region's electorate is astute enough to recognize and stick to its own political vehicle.
"Sisi mlimani tumeamua hakuna siku tutaenda harusi na gari ya mtu mwingine. Sisi tuko na gari yetu sasa ya DCP," Gachagua declared.

The former Deputy President strongly criticized President Ruto's narrative of national equality, branding it a deceptive tactic reminiscent of the 2007 "41 against 1" political mobilization. Gachagua accused the Head of State of tailoring false narratives to different communities—telling Luo voters that previous regimes sidelined them in favor of Mount Kenya, while feeding similar lines to the Somali and Luhya communities. Pointing to the tea sector in Runyenjes and Manyatta, Gachagua argued that Mount Kenya farmers received meager bonuses while Ruto directed KSh 3.7 billion in taxpayer-funded price stabilization money exclusively to tea zones in his Rift Valley backyard, including Bomet, Kericho, and Nandi, leaving out Kiambu, Murang'a, Kirinyaga, Nyeri, Embu, Meru, and Tharaka Nithi.
"Amesema hiyo pesa ipewe watu ya kwao watu ya Bomet, watu ya Kericho, watu ya Nandi. Kiambu, Murang'a, Nyeri, Embu, Meru hakuna chochote," Gachagua noted.

Further challenging the administration's claims of fairness, Gachagua highlighted alleged nepotism in public service appointments and state corporations, claiming the only "equality" achieved under Ruto's government is the uniform deduction of civil servants' payslips. He alleged that out of 5,000 police recruits admitted at the Kiganjo Police Training College, 3,200 came from the President's community while all other Kenyan communities shared the remaining 1,800 slots. He similarly claimed that 27 out of 33 Officers Commanding Stations (OCS) in Nairobi hail from one community, and accused the leadership of the Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen) of prioritizing relatives, warning that such exclusion amounts to a declaration of political war against Mount Kenya.
"Sasa mkisikia hiyo usawa ni sawa mjue ni vita na Mlima Kenya. Naweka soko na wewe ujue tuko na date na wewe next year," he warned.

Turning his focus to county leadership, Gachagua launched a scathing attack on Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, expressing regret for having campaigned for her election and apologizing to Embu residents. He accused the governor of abandoning her county duties to spend months at State House, UDA headquarters, and across Rift Valley counties like Kericho and Nandi strategizing for Ruto's re-election. Gachagua alleged that while local hospitals in Embu lack medicine, roads remain stalled, and a promised water project in Karurumo has failed to materialize, Mbarire was busy distributing mattresses, hospital blankets, gas cylinders, and sacks of money to voters during a by-election in Mbeere North (referred to as Walokalau).
"Hakuna kitu inaendelea Embu. Hospitali hazina dawa. Barabara zimekwama. Pale mbele there is nothing. You are not available," Gachagua said.

Gachagua also faulted Governor Mbarire for failing to champion the interests of Embu tea farmers despite the pressing economic challenges facing the sector. He revealed that he confronted the governor over the 0.8 percent levy imposed on tea and the KSh 12 billion owed to the Kenya Tea Development Agency (KTDA) after the government allegedly failed to honor its fertilizer subsidy pledge, forcing farmers to shoulder the cost through deductions. According to Gachagua, Mbarire dismissed his concerns, stating that her primary focus was securing President Ruto's re-election so that he could reward her with a government job even if Embu voters rejected her.
"Akasema mimi wacha kwanza nifanye kazi ya rais. Rais akirudi mimi sina shida, rais atanipatia kazi," Gachagua recounted.

In light of what he termed a betrayal by the incumbent governor, Gachagua endorsed a young aspirant, Gelonga Mkunji, to unseat Mbarire in the upcoming gubernatorial race. He praised Mkunji for his integrity and loyalty to the community, revealing that the young leader had turned down a KSh 30 million bribe allegedly offered by President Ruto's camp to support Gachagua's impeachment. Urging Embu residents not to dismiss Mkunji because of his youth, Gachagua argued that energetic young leaders who cannot be bought are what the region needs to drive development, while telling Mbarire she was free to relocate to Ruto's Sugoi home.
"Huyu kijana alitiwa pesa na Kasongo 30 million anitoe kwa ofisi akasema hataki. Kama alikataa pesa akula anaweza kula pesa ya watu?" Gachagua asked.

Addressing social issues affecting the youth in Mount Kenya, Gachagua vowed to reinstate the strict crackdown on illicit alcohol and second-generation brews that he spearheaded while in office. He accused the current administration of deliberately flooding the region with lethal brews such as "Katuringui" to destroy young men, challenging the President to distribute the same alcohol in his own home region if he truly believed in equality. Gachagua promised that within ten months of taking power, his administration would ban toxic brews, reduce the number of bars in shopping centers so that butcheries, hotels, and shops outnumber drinking dens, and enforce historical drinking hours starting after work.
"By mwezi ya 10 hiyo gadhuri ngui na hiyo pombe ingine yote tutapiga marafuku. Hatutakubali na hata Mkunji nimemwambia mambo ya vilabu lazima ipunguzwe," he pledged.

Shifting to electoral preparedness, Gachagua issued stern demands to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) chairperson Erastus Ethekon and the commissioners, dismissing vocal government-allied youths as "spoiled brats." He demanded an immediate timeline for the audit of the voters' register to expunge names of deceased persons—citing remarks by Hassan Omar—as well as alleged foreign voters registered from Uganda and Somalia. Gachagua also raised alarm over the expired Smartmatic elections management system contract, questioning how the commission plans to conduct mass voter registration in February without a new system in place.
"Tunauliza wewe chairman wa IEBC tunataka kujua the audit of the voters register itafanywa lini, ndio tutoe majina ya ile watu walikufa," Gachagua demanded.

Gachagua further accused IEBC chairperson Ethekon of taking instructions from Interior Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo, alleging discriminatory practices in the issuance of national identity cards and voter registration. He claimed that while mobile registration units are taken door-to-door in President Ruto's strongholds and regions like North Eastern and Nyanza—with children as young as 14 allegedly receiving IDs within two days—young people in Mount Kenya face delays of up to eight months and are forced to travel to constituency headquarters. Gachagua warned the IEBC chair against allowing Ruto to use him to rig the election, insisting that presidential results must be announced at the constituency level without interference from a national tallying center at Bomas.
"By January you either talk to the leaders or you talk to the people directly, and I want to assure Ethekon don't underrate the determination of Kenyans," he warned.

Responding to President Ruto's recent remarks in Parliament criticizing regional voting blocs, Gachagua mocked the Head of State and told him to save his tears for next year. He confirmed that Mount Kenya has resolved to vote as a unified bloc to remove Ruto from office, uniting voters who previously backed Ruto, those who supported Raila Odinga, undecided voters, and newly registered youth into a formidable eight-million-strong voting bloc. Beyond the sheer numbers, Gachagua emphasized a second, more decisive strategy: achieving a voter turnout of at least 96 percent across the mountain to guarantee Ruto's defeat.
"Tumeamua we are voting as a block na that block ni ya kufukuza wewe uende nyumbani that we have decided so don't panic," Gachagua declared.

Outlining the broader national coalition taking shape against the government, Gachagua asserted that the anti-Ruto wave extends far beyond Mount Kenya. He projected that the opposition will sweep Nairobi's 2.7 million votes, dominate Western Kenya through leaders like Eugene Wamalwa (referred to as Sivuna), secure Kisii, capture the Coast region through Mohamed Ali (Moha), and lock down the Lower Eastern bloc under Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka. With such nationwide consolidation, Gachagua predicted that Ruto's support in Mount Kenya would plummet to between 12 and 14 percent, leaving the opposition with an overwhelming 86 percent victory.
"Si mlima tumeamua, the whole country imeamua. Nairobi 2.7 million yote ni ya kupeleka Kasongo nyumbani," he asserted.

To achieve the targeted 96 percent voter turnout, Gachagua unveiled an elaborate grassroots mobilization plan for election day, August 10. He instructed vehicle owners and boda boda riders to dedicate their transport services to ferrying elderly women and voters to polling stations, adding that even hospitalized patients and individuals in police custody—noting that disgruntled police officers whose pay and insurance were cut are sympathetic to their cause—would be facilitated to cast their ballots. Crucially, Gachagua issued a directive to mothers and local leaders to collect and safely keep the original national ID cards of young men struggling with alcoholism, giving them photocopies for daily use until the morning of the election so no vote is lost.
"All their original IDs must be collected and kept in safe custody na watolewe photocopy watembee nayo, alafu hiyo original tutaitoa asubuhi tarehe 10 mwezi wa nane," he instructed.

While welcoming back Mount Kenya politicians who had previously aligned with President Ruto, Gachagua drew a clear moral line on forgiveness and political rehabilitation. He stated that legislators like Karemba who merely took money from Ruto have been forgiven by the community, provided they return home and seek fresh approval from voters. However, he declared that leaders who allegedly masterminded the storming of churches—citing an incident at Christ the King—or shed the blood of protesters during the Gen Z demonstrations and the Mbeere North by-election would never be forgiven, comparing Ruto's recent actions to the 2007 Kiambaa church tragedy.
"Lakini this time again we cannot forgive him. Tulimsamehe mara ya kwanza. Si ameua Gen Z? Si amesema apigwe risasi mguu? Hatuwezi msamehe," Gachagua stated.

Gachagua also mocked Ruto's planned visit to Embu during the Christmas season, welcoming him to bring sacks of money just as he allegedly did during tours in Kisii and Busia. He urged Embu residents to take the money if offered, noting that taxpayers deserve a share of public funds, while reminding them that taking the cash does not obligate them to vote for the administration. Simultaneously, he ridiculed Public Service Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku (referred to as Rukoo), accusing him of trying to divide the Kikuyu, Embu, and Meru communities—who have been inseparable since the colonial era—before attempting to run for Nairobi Governor where 800,000 Kikuyu voters reside.
"The Kikuyus, the Merus and the Embu are inseparable. Hata wakati ya mkoloni pass ya kutembea ilikuwa ni ya Mkuyu, Mwembu na Mumeru," Gachagua emphasized.

According to Gachagua, senior Mount Kenya ministers serving in Ruto's cabinet have already sensed the impending political defeat and are scrambling to secure county seats as fallback options. He named Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome as preparing to run for Murang'a Governor, Trade Cabinet Secretary Lee Kinyanjui eyeing the Nakuru gubernatorial seat, and Geoffrey Ruku targeting Nairobi, alleging that they are merely draining resources from the President while positioning themselves for post-2027 survival. Gachagua advised Embu gubernatorial hopeful Gelonga Mkunji to carefully manage Ruku should he return to local politics after failing in Nairobi, ensuring he is never placed in a position where he can divide the Mount Kenya community.
"Hawa watu wote ya mlima wako na Kasongo wamesikiza ground wananyonya yeye tu wanaimba pesa ya kwenda kusimama," he remarked.

Concluding his address on a personal note, Gachagua recounted how President Ruto allegedly bribed Members of Parliament to impeach him, expressing deep gratitude to Runyenjes MP Muchangi Karemba for refusing the money and voting against his ouster. Noting that Embu hosted his last public function as Deputy President and his first after leaving office, Gachagua pledged to camp in the county during the election period—even if it meant sleeping in his car or bathing from a basin—to ensure DCP sweeps all seats from Governor to MCAs. He announced a meeting the following week at Monyoro for all DCP aspirants to prepare for free and fair party primaries in March, urging candidates to rally behind women voters before the church service concluded with a fundraiser.
"Governor hapa atakuwa wa DCP, senator wa DCP, women rep wa DCP, wabunge wote wanne DCP, MCAs wote 20 of them," Gachagua concluded.

Kenya and DRC Agree to Restore Ambassadorial Ties After Two Years of Diplomatic Fallout
items.description: Kenya and DRC have agreed to restore ambassadorial relations after years of diplomatic tensions linked to the M23 conflict.
content: Kenya and DRC have agreed to restore ambassadorial relations after years of diplomatic tensions linked to the M23 conflict.

Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have agreed to restore full ambassadorial relations after more than two years of diplomatic tensions that strained ties between the neighbouring East African Community (EAC) members.

President William Ruto announced the breakthrough on November 22, 2026, following a Quadripartite Political Summit in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, where he held discussions with DRC President Felix Tshisekedi and other regional leaders.

The agreement provides for the restoration of diplomatic representation at ambassadorial level, the resumption of the Joint Grand Commission for Cooperation and regular consultations between the two governments.
The development marks a significant step towards repairing relations that deteriorated after Kinshasa accused Nairobi of allowing M23 rebel leaders to operate politically from Kenya.
The diplomatic fallout resulted in the recall of envoys, disagreements over ambassadorial appointments and an attack on the Kenyan Embassy in Kinshasa.
Ruto said the two countries had committed themselves to fully normalising relations and rebuilding cooperation across several areas of mutual interest.

"We committed to working towards fully restoring diplomatic relations, including restoring representation at ambassadorial level, resuming the Joint Grand Commission for Cooperation and strengthening regular diplomatic consultations," Ruto stated.
Under the agreement, the DRC will also restore its ambassadorial representation in Nairobi, addressing the diplomatic imbalance that followed the deterioration of relations.
The diplomatic crisis between Nairobi and Kinshasa emerged amid escalating tensions over the conflict in eastern DRC, where government forces have been fighting the M23 rebel movement.
Relations deteriorated after the DRC government accused Kenya of providing a platform for M23 leaders, allegations that Nairobi faced amid its diplomatic and regional engagement efforts.
Kinshasa subsequently recalled its diplomatic officials from Nairobi, although its envoy briefly returned in mid-2024.
However, the return did not result in a complete restoration of ambassadorial relations between the two countries.
The disagreement continued to affect diplomatic representation and cooperation, creating uncertainty over the future of bilateral relations.
In January 2025, the diplomatic dispute escalated after rioters attacked and looted the Kenyan Embassy in Kinshasa.
The protesters accused Kenya of involvement in the conflict in eastern DRC, further complicating efforts to repair relations between the two governments.
The incident prompted the Kenyan government to condemn the attack and demand action over the safety of its diplomatic personnel and property.
The disagreement also affected Kenya's efforts to establish full diplomatic representation in Kinshasa.
In early 2025, Ruto appointed Peter Tum as Kenya's ambassador to the DRC.
However, the Congolese government withheld accreditation, preventing Tum from formally taking up the position as Kenya's confirmed top diplomatic representative in the country.
The latest agreement now provides an opportunity to resolve the outstanding diplomatic issues and restore normal government-to-government engagement.
The Oyo summit brought together Ruto, Tshisekedi, Republic of the Congo President Denis Sassou N'Guesso and Togo President Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé.
The discussions focused on rebuilding diplomatic relations, strengthening economic partnerships and addressing regional security challenges.
Kenya and the DRC also agreed to deepen cooperation in trade, economic development, security and cultural exchange.
Ruto said the two governments had committed to working together to promote regional peace, stability and integration.
"We also agreed to deepen cooperation in trade, economic development, security and culture while working together to advance regional peace, stability and integration," he added.
The discussions come at a time when both countries have an interest in strengthening economic and political cooperation within the East African Community.
The DRC joined the regional bloc in 2022, creating opportunities for expanded trade, investment and cross-border economic activities.
Kenya has maintained strategic economic and diplomatic interests in the Congolese market, particularly in trade, banking, logistics and regional infrastructure.
Restoring ambassadorial relations could therefore help remove diplomatic obstacles affecting cooperation between the two countries.

The resumption of the Joint Grand Commission for Cooperation will also provide a formal platform for government officials to address bilateral challenges, review existing agreements and identify new areas of partnership.
However, the success of the agreement will depend on whether both governments follow through on their commitments, particularly the restoration of diplomatic representation and regular consultations.
For Nairobi and Kinshasa, rebuilding trust will be critical after years of disagreements over regional security and the conflict involving M23 in eastern DRC.
The latest breakthrough offers both countries an opportunity to move beyond the diplomatic fallout and strengthen their relationship as members of the East African Community.

items.title: Ruto and Tshisekedi agree to restore Kenya-DRC diplomatic ties
items.description: The Oyo summit produced a pledge to restore ambassador-level ties, but the reports give no timetable for putting the agreement into effect.
content: The Oyo summit produced a pledge to restore ambassador-level ties, but the reports give no timetable for putting the agreement into effect.

Kenya and the Democratic Republic of the Congo agreed to restore diplomatic representation at ambassador level, resume their Joint Grand Commission for Cooperation and hold regular consultations, President William Ruto said after meeting Félix Tshisekedi in Oyo on Sunday.

The agreement came at a four-country summit in the Republic of the Congo, bringing together Kenya, the host country, the DRC and Togo. The dispute between Nairobi and Kinshasa had strained relations since late 2023, when the DRC objected to the launch in Nairobi of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, a political-military coalition linked to the M23 rebellion. Kinshasa recalled its ambassador; Kenya said it could not restrict political expression.

Ruto and Tshisekedi also committed to cooperation in trade, security, economic development and culture , according to The Star’s account of the post-meeting statement. Ruto said the engagement would be guided by dialogue and mutual respect. The leaders were hosted by Republic of the Congo President Denis Sassou-N’Guesso, with Togo’s Faure Gnassingbé participating as a regional mediator.

The first reports, filed before the summit, described its purpose as expected rather than settled. The Standard and People Daily said the leaders were due to discuss diplomatic ties, regional security, peacebuilding and economic cooperation. People Daily noted that a detailed official agenda had not been publicly released at that point.

TUKO likewise reported before the meeting that the specific agenda was undisclosed, and said the full attendee list had not been officially confirmed when it published. The Standard and People Daily named all four leaders expected to attend. The Star’s later report supplied the outcome those earlier accounts could not: Ruto and Tshisekedi had agreed on practical steps to restore government-to-government ties.

The Star’s earlier report and The Standard both set out the roots of the falling-out. They cited the December 2023 AFC launch in Nairobi and a further deterioration after a gathering of Congolese opposition figures in Nairobi in October 2025. People Daily also identified former DRC president Joseph Kabila among those involved in the later gathering. Kenya’s defence, as reported by The Star, was that it had not participated in the event and could not bar political expression.

The Star offered the clearest account of the economic stakes: eastern DRC uses the Port of Mombasa and the Northern Corridor as a trade route, while Kenyan financial institutions also have business interests in the DRC. That makes the restoration of diplomatic channels relevant beyond the two governments’ political dispute.

The Standard placed the summit within a broader sequence of regional diplomacy, recalling an Oyo meeting in 2022 and a Quadripartite Summit in Luanda in 2023. It also described Gnassingbé as the African Union-appointed mediator in the eastern DRC conflict. The Star’s account said he mediated the talks, while noting that the AU appointed him to the eastern DRC peace process in April 2025.

Ruto’s travel interrupted a Western Kenya development tour. The Kenya Times gave the most detailed itinerary, listing engagements in Busia and Bungoma before his departure and saying the tour’s second phase was scheduled for November 28 to December 1 . People Daily and TUKO reported that he left via Kisumu International Airport; TUKO characterised the departure as secretive, while the other accounts focused on the summit and its diplomatic purpose.

What remains open is how quickly the promised ambassadorial appointments and cooperation commission will be put in place. The reports give no timetable, and the agreement itself does not settle the wider dispute over political activity linked to armed groups. The next test is whether the leaders’ commitment to consultation produces regular contact and changes in how Nairobi and Kinshasa handle those disagreements.
The second phase of Ruto’s Western Kenya tour is scheduled to resume.
The Kenya Times reported the dates and counties planned for the continuation of the tour.

Gachagua Promises Mt Kenya Political Direction Before Christmas Break
items.description: Rigathi Gachagua says Mt Kenya residents will decide their 2027 political direction during Christmas gatherings, with consultations covering all elective seats.
content: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua says the Mt Kenya region will settle on its political direction for the 2027 General Election during the Christmas holidays.

Speaking at a church service at Wonders of God in Karurumo, Runyenjes, Embu County, on Sunday, November 22, 2026, Gachagua said families and community members would discuss candidates for various elective positions during the festive season.

He said the consultations would cover the presidency, governor, senator, woman representative, Members of Parliament, and Members of County Assembly. Gachagua added that people in the region traditionally make political decisions during Christmas gatherings.

“Tukienda uchaguzi mwaka ujao every year, every five years, maamuzi hapa mlimani tunafanya wakati wa Krismasi. Si Krismasi iko karibu? Si mnang’oa maneno? Kuanzia 23rd, 24th, 25th. By 26th Boxing Day, maneno imekwisha,” Gachagua said.
He said people returning to their rural homes from Nairobi and other towns would discuss the region’s political choices with their families before reaching a consensus.

“Watu ya Nairobi wamekuja, kila mtu watu wamekaa kwa familia wameongea, ‘Ehe, hii kareba inakaa namna gani? Tuangushe ama tupitishe?’ Wanaongea, wanakubaliana. ‘Hii gavana iko namna gani?’ Wanaongea, wanakubaliana. ‘Hii MCA nani, nani, nani, nani?’ ” he said.
The Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader urged Mt Kenya residents who still support President William Ruto’s political camp to return home and take part in the anticipated discussions.
Gachagua warned that residents who stayed away could end up on the losing side once the community chose its preferred candidates.
“Kwa hivyo wale mungali mko kwa Kasongo, decision ya mlima ya vile uchaguzi wa mwaka ujao utakaa, kuanzia kiti ya Rais, gavana, seneta, women rep, MP, MCA, itafanywa hii Krismas,” he said.
He also encouraged residents with political ambitions to attend the Christmas gatherings, saying the discussions would help shape the region’s electoral position.

Gachagua said he planned to issue political direction for Mt Kenya before the Christmas break, giving residents time to discuss his position with their families. He said he expected them to review the proposal and report back after the holiday.
“Before twende Christmas, 22nd, 23rd, lazima pia nitoe mwelekeo hapa mlimani ndio muende muongee wakati ya Christmas. Ikifika 27, 28 mnirudishie ripoti,” he said.
He said his political direction would reflect his assessment of sentiment on the ground, while leaving room for residents to propose changes.
“So I want to promise before we break for Christmas, we shall give political direction for this region so that tukikula Christmas tukubaliane vizuri,” Gachagua said.

The Sacco Societies Regulatory Authority (SASRA) has published its Sacco Supervision Annual Report 2025 , revealing the full ranking of Kenya's largest deposit-taking SACCOs by total assets and exposing a sharp concentration of wealth among the top institutions.
Mwalimu National DT has held on to its position as Kenya's largest SACCO, recording total assets of KSh 76.31 billion in 2025, up from KSh 68.89 billion the previous year.
Stima DT, however, has mounted a serious challenge, expanding its asset base from KSh 66.51 billion to KSh 75.27 billion, leaving only a KSh 1 billion gap between the two giants.

Kenya National Police DT occupies third position with KSh 66.40 billion in assets, while Harambee DT holds fourth place at KSh 41.29 billion.
Below Harambee, a gap of approximately KSh 6.7 billion separates the top four from the rest of the rankings, with Tower DT entering at fifth place with KSh 34.56 billion.

Unaitas (6th) and Imarisha (7th) both recorded growth, posting assets of KSh 29.60 billion and KSh 28.14 billion, respectively. Afya DT, ranked eighth, was the only institution in the top 10 to record a decline, with assets slipping from KSh 22.79 billion to KSh 21.95 billion.

Positions 11 through 20 form a tightly contested band, with all institutions holding assets between KSh 14 billion and KSh 18 billion. Winas (14th), Apstar DT (15th), Invest and Grow (16th), Imarika (17th), and Bandari DT (18th) range from KSh 16.90 billion down to KSh 15.07 billion.

Qona DT (19th) and Boresha DT (20th) close out the list at KSh 14.80 billion and KSh 14.70 billion, respectively, meaning any SACCO outside the top 20 would need to surpass that KSh 14.70 billion threshold to break into the elite tier.

The 2025 data signals that Kenya's cooperative sector is increasingly dominated by its largest players, with the top 20 SACCOs collectively holding well above half a trillion shillings in combined assets, raising the bar for smaller institutions hoping to compete at the highest level.

items.description: UK Seasonal Worker visa applications offer Kenyans up to six months’ farm work, but £340 fees, upfront costs and exploitation risks demand careful consideration.
content: Search option is now available at TUKO! Feel free to search the content on topics/people you enjoy reading about in the top right corner ;)
The United Kingdom has reopened its Seasonal Worker visa programme, allowing foreign nationals, including Kenyans, to take up temporary agricultural roles lasting as long as six months.

The scheme targets labour shortages on British farms during peak harvesting periods and the Christmas poultry season, and it operates exclusively through a network of government-approved scheme operators.
Two sectors qualify under the programme. Horticulture positions span a wide range of produce, from soft fruits such as strawberries and orchard crops to mushrooms, cut flowers, and tree nurseries.
UK confirms how foreigners including Kenyans can work as farmers
PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.

The poultry route covers twelve specific roles, including butcher, poultry processor, poultry catcher, and food operative, though it is restricted to workers arriving between October 2 and December 31 each year, with applications closing no later than 15 November.
For the 2026 and 2027 seasons, the annual quota stands at 41,000 slots for horticulture and 1,900 for poultry.
The scheme has been extended through 2029 to give growers and operators greater planning certainty.

Applicants must pay a £340 (approximately KSh 61,200) visa fee and demonstrate access to at least £1,270 (approximately KSh 227,700) in savings held for a minimum of 28 consecutive days unless their sponsor certifies maintenance.

No immigration health surcharge applies given the visa's duration. Workers are bound to the job listed in their certificate of sponsorship, cannot access public funds, and may not bring family members.
The financial appeal for Kenyan workers is considerable.
Austria recruiting cold season workers: Free accommodation, salary up to KSh 332k

The UK national minimum wage for agricultural workers aged 21 and over is £12.71 per hour, equivalent to roughly KSh 2,270, compared with Kenya's general labour minimum wage of approximately KSh 15,200 per month.
Farm-provided accommodation is typically deducted at around £77 (KSh 13,800) per week.

The Kenyan government has promoted the route through the Mkulima Majuu programme, with the State Department for Diaspora Affairs partnering HOPS Labour Solutions and the Youth Enterprise Development Fund to recruit from agricultural colleges and polytechnics, including Bukura Agricultural College and Sigalagala National Polytechnic.

The scheme's structure poses documented risks. Because workers are tied to a single sponsoring operator and their accommodation depends on that employer, labour rights researchers have consistently flagged the power imbalance as a vulnerability.

A 2026 academic study concluded that the Seasonal Worker visa's design "compounded by the effects of the cessation of EU Freedom of Movement led to heightened risks of labour exploitation" and noted that workers had paid fees to secure placements.
Advocacy groups warn that recruitment-related debts, combined with the single-employer tie, heighten the risk of modern slavery.
UK Embassy Kenya announces deadline to apply for 2027 fully funded Commonwealth scholarships
Upfront costs remain a practical barrier. Beyond the visa fee and savings requirement, applicants must fund their own airfare.

Kenyans seeking a placement should approach only licensed scheme operators, which issues the certificate of sponsorship required to submit an online application. Any agent promising a visa without that document should be treated as a fraud risk.

items.description: Konza Technopolis has been designated a Customs Area and allocated a customs code by the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), paving the way for faster movement of goods and simplified customs procedures for
content: Konza Technopolis has been designated a Customs Area and allocated a customs code by the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), paving the way for faster movement of goods and simplified customs procedures for businesses operating within the smart city.

The designation marks a major step towards making Konza’s Special Economic Zone (SEZ) fully operational, particularly for companies involved in manufacturing, technology development and other businesses that depend on importing and exporting goods.
The development is expected to reduce customs-related delays and improve the ease of doing business, making Konza more attractive to local and international investors.
Technopolis Development Authority Chief Executive Officer John Paul Okwiri said the new status addresses a key requirement for businesses seeking to establish operations within the zone.

“The gazettement of Konza Technopolis as a Customs Area and the allocation of a customs code is a significant step towards making our Special Economic Zone fully operational. It will facilitate the movement of goods, simplify customs processes and create a more enabling environment for investors,” said Okwiri.
Konza Technopolis was gazetted as a Special Economic Zone in July 2019 as part of Kenya’s efforts to attract investment in technology, innovation and industrial development.
The latest approval strengthens the regulatory framework needed to support businesses operating within the smart city and advances Kenya’s ambition to become a knowledge-based economy.

items.title: "It's immoral": Governors reject PS Oluga's order to remove hospital paybills
items.description: Kenya’s Council of Governors challenges Ouma Oluga’s order to remove county hospital Paybill numbers, citing SHA coverage gaps and devolution rights in counties.
content: PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
Amos Khaemba is a Current Affairs Editor at TUKO.co.ke, covering general news. Khaemba has over four years of journalism experience and joined TUKO.co.ke in 2022.

Nairobi - The Council of Governors (CoG) has come out strongly against a directive issued by the Principal Secretary for Medical Services, Ouma Oluga, instructing county health facilities to deactivate their Paybill numbers, describing the order as unconstitutional and a direct assault on the autonomy of county governments.

In a statement released on Monday, November 23, the CoG acknowledged the broader goal of shielding patients from double charges on services fully funded by the Social Health Authority (SHA), but argued that the PS's directive failed to account for the realities facing county facilities on the ground.

The Council noted that SHA coverage does not extend to every Kenyan or to the full range of healthcare services offered at county facilities.

Certain services fall outside the authority's approved benefits package, and delayed, rejected, or insufficient reimbursements from SHA have continued to place serious financial strain on county health facilities across the country.
Removing Paybill numbers, the CoG warned, would strip county governments of a lawful mechanism for recovering costs and sustaining day-to-day service delivery.

The Council consequently directed all health facility managers to disregard the PS's instruction entirely, maintaining that county governments must retain the right to collect payments for services not covered or not yet reimbursed under the SHA framework.
South C residents raise alarm over condition of 15-storey apartment next to collapsed building

The CoG framed the standoff not merely as an administrative dispute but as a constitutional matter, arguing that the directive by Oluga cuts across the devolved functions assigned to county governments under Kenya's constitution.

The Council's position is that decisions over cost-recovery mechanisms within county health facilities fall within the mandate of county governments, and cannot be overridden by a directive from a national government official.

Nancy Odindo is a Current Affairs Editor at TUKO.co.ke, covering general news. Odindo has over six years of journalism experience and joined TUKO.co.ke in 2023.

The Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) has shifted its 95th Graduation Ceremony from Thursday, December 3, 2026 to Friday, December 4, 2026, following an official announcement by the institution's Chief Executive Officer.
KMTC CEO Dr. Kelly Oluoch issued the public notice on Monday, November 23, 2026, alerting students and other stakeholders to the revised schedule.
The ceremony will be held at Moi International Sports Centre, Kasarani , Nairobi, beginning at 8am under the theme "Mashujaa wa Afya."

Alongside the ceremony date change, the graduation rehearsal has also been rescheduled.
Students will now attend rehearsals on Thursday, December 3, 2026, at the same venue and at the same start time of 8am, a day ahead of the main event.
The deadline for gown collection has been extended to Monday, November 30, 2026. Students are required to collect their gowns from KMTC headquarters in Nairobi before that date.

Graduating students will be able to collect their certificates between December 7 and December 16, 2026, on weekdays between 9am and 4pm at KMTC headquarters. Collection remains subject to completion of all clearance requirements.
KMTC has urged students to take note of all the revised dates and make the necessary arrangements ahead of the ceremony.
Further information is available on the college's official website at www.kmtc.ac.ke or via its social media handle @KMTCOfficial.

items.title: Gachagua Announces December Political Direction for Mt. Kenya and Endorses Gelonga Mkunji for Embu Governor
items.description: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua addressed congregants during a church service at Wonders of God Church in Runyenjes, Embu County, where he outlined...
content: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua addressed congregants during a church service at Wonders of God Church in Runyenjes, Embu County, where he outlined a m...

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua addressed congregants during a church service at Wonders of God Church in Runyenjes, Embu County, where he outlined a major political realignment for the Mount Kenya region ahead of the upcoming general election. Gachagua welcomed Runyenjes Member of Parliament Muchangi Karemba back to the regional fold, noting that Karemba had listened to the sentiments of his constituents on the ground and decided to abandon President William Ruto's political camp. Emphasizing that all politics is local, Gachagua praised Karemba, alongside lawmakers Kagombe and Gathoni Wamuchomba (referred to as Mkami), for resonating with the desires of their electorate rather than remaining tied to political arrangements in Nairobi.
"What a clever leader does, you listen to your people and these are your people. All politics is local hapa mlimani," Gachagua stated.

Gachagua announced that the Mount Kenya region will make its definitive political decisions for the next election during the upcoming Christmas festivities, between December 23 and Boxing Day on December 26. He explained that residents working in Nairobi and elsewhere will travel home to consult with their families and agree on preferred candidates for every elective seat, from the presidency down to Members of County Assemblies. Ahead of the holiday break, Gachagua pledged to issue a clear political direction on December 22 or 23, asking residents to deliberate on his guidance over Christmas and report back with any proposed adjustments by December 27 or 28.
"So promise before we break for Christmas, we shall give political direction for this region so that tukikula Christmas tukubaliane vizuri," he said.

Reflecting on past political alliances, Gachagua used the metaphor of hiring a vehicle for a wedding only to be abandoned along the way to describe the region's fallout with President Ruto. He declared that the Mount Kenya electorate has resolved never again to rely on another leader's political vehicle, announcing that they now have their own green-colored party, the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), which he described as the color of restoration and prosperity. Dismissing rival political outfits—including Ruto's yellow party and smaller parties being introduced in Runyenjes and Manyatta to confuse voters—Gachagua insisted that the region's electorate is astute enough to recognize and stick to its own political vehicle.
"Sisi mlimani tumeamua hakuna siku tutaenda harusi na gari ya mtu mwingine. Sisi tuko na gari yetu sasa ya DCP," Gachagua declared.

The former Deputy President strongly criticized President Ruto's narrative of national equality, branding it a deceptive tactic reminiscent of the 2007 "41 against 1" political mobilization. Gachagua accused the Head of State of tailoring false narratives to different communities—telling Luo voters that previous regimes sidelined them in favor of Mount Kenya, while feeding similar lines to the Somali and Luhya communities. Pointing to the tea sector in Runyenjes and Manyatta, Gachagua argued that Mount Kenya farmers received meager bonuses while Ruto directed KSh 3.7 billion in taxpayer-funded price stabilization money exclusively to tea zones in his Rift Valley backyard, including Bomet, Kericho, and Nandi, leaving out Kiambu, Murang'a, Kirinyaga, Nyeri, Embu, Meru, and Tharaka Nithi.
"Amesema hiyo pesa ipewe watu ya kwao watu ya Bomet, watu ya Kericho, watu ya Nandi. Kiambu, Murang'a, Nyeri, Embu, Meru hakuna chochote," Gachagua noted.

Further challenging the administration's claims of fairness, Gachagua highlighted alleged nepotism in public service appointments and state corporations, claiming the only "equality" achieved under Ruto's government is the uniform deduction of civil servants' payslips. He alleged that out of 5,000 police recruits admitted at the Kiganjo Police Training College, 3,200 came from the President's community while all other Kenyan communities shared the remaining 1,800 slots. He similarly claimed that 27 out of 33 Officers Commanding Stations (OCS) in Nairobi hail from one community, and accused the leadership of the Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen) of prioritizing relatives, warning that such exclusion amounts to a declaration of political war against Mount Kenya.
"Sasa mkisikia hiyo usawa ni sawa mjue ni vita na Mlima Kenya. Naweka soko na wewe ujue tuko na date na wewe next year," he warned.

Turning his focus to county leadership, Gachagua launched a scathing attack on Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, expressing regret for having campaigned for her election and apologizing to Embu residents. He accused the governor of abandoning her county duties to spend months at State House, UDA headquarters, and across Rift Valley counties like Kericho and Nandi strategizing for Ruto's re-election. Gachagua alleged that while local hospitals in Embu lack medicine, roads remain stalled, and a promised water project in Karurumo has failed to materialize, Mbarire was busy distributing mattresses, hospital blankets, gas cylinders, and sacks of money to voters during a by-election in Mbeere North (referred to as Walokalau).
"Hakuna kitu inaendelea Embu. Hospitali hazina dawa. Barabara zimekwama. Pale mbele there is nothing. You are not available," Gachagua said.

Gachagua also faulted Governor Mbarire for failing to champion the interests of Embu tea farmers despite the pressing economic challenges facing the sector. He revealed that he confronted the governor over the 0.8 percent levy imposed on tea and the KSh 12 billion owed to the Kenya Tea Development Agency (KTDA) after the government allegedly failed to honor its fertilizer subsidy pledge, forcing farmers to shoulder the cost through deductions. According to Gachagua, Mbarire dismissed his concerns, stating that her primary focus was securing President Ruto's re-election so that he could reward her with a government job even if Embu voters rejected her.
"Akasema mimi wacha kwanza nifanye kazi ya rais. Rais akirudi mimi sina shida, rais atanipatia kazi," Gachagua recounted.

In light of what he termed a betrayal by the incumbent governor, Gachagua endorsed a young aspirant, Gelonga Mkunji, to unseat Mbarire in the upcoming gubernatorial race. He praised Mkunji for his integrity and loyalty to the community, revealing that the young leader had turned down a KSh 30 million bribe allegedly offered by President Ruto's camp to support Gachagua's impeachment. Urging Embu residents not to dismiss Mkunji because of his youth, Gachagua argued that energetic young leaders who cannot be bought are what the region needs to drive development, while telling Mbarire she was free to relocate to Ruto's Sugoi home.
"Huyu kijana alitiwa pesa na Kasongo 30 million anitoe kwa ofisi akasema hataki. Kama alikataa pesa akula anaweza kula pesa ya watu?" Gachagua asked.

Addressing social issues affecting the youth in Mount Kenya, Gachagua vowed to reinstate the strict crackdown on illicit alcohol and second-generation brews that he spearheaded while in office. He accused the current administration of deliberately flooding the region with lethal brews such as "Katuringui" to destroy young men, challenging the President to distribute the same alcohol in his own home region if he truly believed in equality. Gachagua promised that within ten months of taking power, his administration would ban toxic brews, reduce the number of bars in shopping centers so that butcheries, hotels, and shops outnumber drinking dens, and enforce historical drinking hours starting after work.
"By mwezi ya 10 hiyo gadhuri ngui na hiyo pombe ingine yote tutapiga marafuku. Hatutakubali na hata Mkunji nimemwambia mambo ya vilabu lazima ipunguzwe," he pledged.

Shifting to electoral preparedness, Gachagua issued stern demands to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) chairperson Erastus Ethekon and the commissioners, dismissing vocal government-allied youths as "spoiled brats." He demanded an immediate timeline for the audit of the voters' register to expunge names of deceased persons—citing remarks by Hassan Omar—as well as alleged foreign voters registered from Uganda and Somalia. Gachagua also raised alarm over the expired Smartmatic elections management system contract, questioning how the commission plans to conduct mass voter registration in February without a new system in place.
"Tunauliza wewe chairman wa IEBC tunataka kujua the audit of the voters register itafanywa lini, ndio tutoe majina ya ile watu walikufa," Gachagua demanded.

Gachagua further accused IEBC chairperson Ethekon of taking instructions from Interior Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo, alleging discriminatory practices in the issuance of national identity cards and voter registration. He claimed that while mobile registration units are taken door-to-door in President Ruto's strongholds and regions like North Eastern and Nyanza—with children as young as 14 allegedly receiving IDs within two days—young people in Mount Kenya face delays of up to eight months and are forced to travel to constituency headquarters. Gachagua warned the IEBC chair against allowing Ruto to use him to rig the election, insisting that presidential results must be announced at the constituency level without interference from a national tallying center at Bomas.
"By January you either talk to the leaders or you talk to the people directly, and I want to assure Ethekon don't underrate the determination of Kenyans," he warned.

Responding to President Ruto's recent remarks in Parliament criticizing regional voting blocs, Gachagua mocked the Head of State and told him to save his tears for next year. He confirmed that Mount Kenya has resolved to vote as a unified bloc to remove Ruto from office, uniting voters who previously backed Ruto, those who supported Raila Odinga, undecided voters, and newly registered youth into a formidable eight-million-strong voting bloc. Beyond the sheer numbers, Gachagua emphasized a second, more decisive strategy: achieving a voter turnout of at least 96 percent across the mountain to guarantee Ruto's defeat.
"Tumeamua we are voting as a block na that block ni ya kufukuza wewe uende nyumbani that we have decided so don't panic," Gachagua declared.

Outlining the broader national coalition taking shape against the government, Gachagua asserted that the anti-Ruto wave extends far beyond Mount Kenya. He projected that the opposition will sweep Nairobi's 2.7 million votes, dominate Western Kenya through leaders like Eugene Wamalwa (referred to as Sivuna), secure Kisii, capture the Coast region through Mohamed Ali (Moha), and lock down the Lower Eastern bloc under Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka. With such nationwide consolidation, Gachagua predicted that Ruto's support in Mount Kenya would plummet to between 12 and 14 percent, leaving the opposition with an overwhelming 86 percent victory.
"Si mlima tumeamua, the whole country imeamua. Nairobi 2.7 million yote ni ya kupeleka Kasongo nyumbani," he asserted.

To achieve the targeted 96 percent voter turnout, Gachagua unveiled an elaborate grassroots mobilization plan for election day, August 10. He instructed vehicle owners and boda boda riders to dedicate their transport services to ferrying elderly women and voters to polling stations, adding that even hospitalized patients and individuals in police custody—noting that disgruntled police officers whose pay and insurance were cut are sympathetic to their cause—would be facilitated to cast their ballots. Crucially, Gachagua issued a directive to mothers and local leaders to collect and safely keep the original national ID cards of young men struggling with alcoholism, giving them photocopies for daily use until the morning of the election so no vote is lost.
"All their original IDs must be collected and kept in safe custody na watolewe photocopy watembee nayo, alafu hiyo original tutaitoa asubuhi tarehe 10 mwezi wa nane," he instructed.

While welcoming back Mount Kenya politicians who had previously aligned with President Ruto, Gachagua drew a clear moral line on forgiveness and political rehabilitation. He stated that legislators like Karemba who merely took money from Ruto have been forgiven by the community, provided they return home and seek fresh approval from voters. However, he declared that leaders who allegedly masterminded the storming of churches—citing an incident at Christ the King—or shed the blood of protesters during the Gen Z demonstrations and the Mbeere North by-election would never be forgiven, comparing Ruto's recent actions to the 2007 Kiambaa church tragedy.
"Lakini this time again we cannot forgive him. Tulimsamehe mara ya kwanza. Si ameua Gen Z? Si amesema apigwe risasi mguu? Hatuwezi msamehe," Gachagua stated.

Gachagua also mocked Ruto's planned visit to Embu during the Christmas season, welcoming him to bring sacks of money just as he allegedly did during tours in Kisii and Busia. He urged Embu residents to take the money if offered, noting that taxpayers deserve a share of public funds, while reminding them that taking the cash does not obligate them to vote for the administration. Simultaneously, he ridiculed Public Service Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku (referred to as Rukoo), accusing him of trying to divide the Kikuyu, Embu, and Meru communities—who have been inseparable since the colonial era—before attempting to run for Nairobi Governor where 800,000 Kikuyu voters reside.
"The Kikuyus, the Merus and the Embu are inseparable. Hata wakati ya mkoloni pass ya kutembea ilikuwa ni ya Mkuyu, Mwembu na Mumeru," Gachagua emphasized.

According to Gachagua, senior Mount Kenya ministers serving in Ruto's cabinet have already sensed the impending political defeat and are scrambling to secure county seats as fallback options. He named Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome as preparing to run for Murang'a Governor, Trade Cabinet Secretary Lee Kinyanjui eyeing the Nakuru gubernatorial seat, and Geoffrey Ruku targeting Nairobi, alleging that they are merely draining resources from the President while positioning themselves for post-2027 survival. Gachagua advised Embu gubernatorial hopeful Gelonga Mkunji to carefully manage Ruku should he return to local politics after failing in Nairobi, ensuring he is never placed in a position where he can divide the Mount Kenya community.
"Hawa watu wote ya mlima wako na Kasongo wamesikiza ground wananyonya yeye tu wanaimba pesa ya kwenda kusimama," he remarked.

Concluding his address on a personal note, Gachagua recounted how President Ruto allegedly bribed Members of Parliament to impeach him, expressing deep gratitude to Runyenjes MP Muchangi Karemba for refusing the money and voting against his ouster. Noting that Embu hosted his last public function as Deputy President and his first after leaving office, Gachagua pledged to camp in the county during the election period—even if it meant sleeping in his car or bathing from a basin—to ensure DCP sweeps all seats from Governor to MCAs. He announced a meeting the following week at Monyoro for all DCP aspirants to prepare for free and fair party primaries in March, urging candidates to rally behind women voters before the church service concluded with a fundraiser.
"Governor hapa atakuwa wa DCP, senator wa DCP, women rep wa DCP, wabunge wote wanne DCP, MCAs wote 20 of them," Gachagua concluded.

Inaugural Sisibo Marathon to pay each winner record Sh5m
items.description: Handsome prize money awaits competitors in the first edition of the race in Eldoret.
content: From left: New York Marathon Champion Sheila Chepkirui multiple Olympics and world champion Faith Kipyegon, Uasin Gishu County Governor Jonathan Bii, former 5,000m Commonwealth Games champion Mercy Cherono, President William Ruto's aide Farouk Kibet, Athletics Kenya President Jack Tuwei, Tokyo Marathon champion Rosemary Wanjiru, and former 800m world champion Janeth Jepkogei, during the launch of Sisibo Marathonin Eldoret, Uasin Gishu County on November 22, 2026.
Local athletes will fight for a share of Sh25 million prize purse in the inaugural edition of Sisibo Marathon.

Speaking on Sunday during the launch at Lobo Village in Eldoret, organisers said winners of men and women’s categories in the inaugural edition planned for December 19, 2026 in Eldoret, will each take home Sh5 million, the highest locally.

Runners-up will take home Sh3 million, with third-place finishers earning Sh1 million. The top 20 finishers in every category will get cash awards, with the fourth-placed finishers taking home Sh700,000.
Cash prizes will trickle down to the top 10 athletes, with the 10th-placed runners in both categories pocketing Sh150,000. Registration will be free of charge for all participants.
Read: Sheila Chepkirui: I won New York Marathon by focusing on strength, nutrition

The prize money makes Sisibo Marathon the highest paying locally, followed by Nairobi City Marathon and Eldoret City Marathon. Winners of Nairobi City Marathon are paid Sh3.5 million each, while second and third-placed take home Sh2.25 million and 1.5 million respectively.
Each winner at the Eldoret City Marathon takes home Sh3.5 million, while second and third-placed finishers get Sh1.5 million and Sh1 million in that order.
Standard Chartered Nairobi Marathon awards winners cash prize of Sh2 million, while runners-up take home Sh1 million, and second runners-up Sh500,000.
On Sunday, National Olympic Committee of Kenya (NOC-K) First Vice President Barnaba Korir said the race is expected to attract more than 2,000 elite athletes.

“This is going to be a race of its kind in the country. Athletes will share a prize kitty of more than Sh25 million, with the men’s and women’s champions walking away with Sh5 million each,” said Korir.
Two-time Olympics marathon Champion Eliud Kipchoge makes his remarks during the launch of Sisibo Marathon in Eldoret, Uasin Gishu County on November 22, 2026.

Two-time Olympics marathon champion Eliud Kipchoge thanked the government and organisers for bringing a high-stakes race to Eldoret which is popularly known as “city of champions,” and urged corporates to support it so it can rival major races globally.
“The Sisibo Marathon has the potential to grow into a premier international marathon and put Eldoret even better on the global athletics map,” said Kipchoge.
Conversations around athlete welfare, doping, and financial management of local athletics dominated the speeches.
Read: 'So shameful': Top Kenyan runners dismayed over Jepchirchir doping case

President William Ruto’s aide, Farouk Kibet, challenged the government to exempt athletes from taxes and appoint former sports personalities to key administrative roles to better safeguard athlete welfare.

“It is sad that our athletes bring fame to our country, yet in retirement, they are living in abject poverty because they squandered their earnings instead of investing it for the future,” Kibet said.
He urged the Ministry of Roads to construct dedicated training lanes for athletes to use on roads to curb road accidents involving runners.

From left: President William Ruto's aide Farouk Kibet, Athletics Kenya President Jack Tuwei and and three-time Boston Marathon champion Ibrahim Hussein, during the launch of Sisibo Marathon in Eldoret, Uasin Gishu County on November 22, 2026.
Athletics Kenya President Lt. Gen. (Rtd) Jackson Tuwei urged local athletes to emulate their Ethiopian counterparts by exercising financial discipline.
Tuwei also issued a stern warning to athletes who engage in doping, noting that a single positive test erases years of hard-won glory.
“It is painful to see athletes win races across the globe, only to water everything down by engaging in doping,” said Tuwei.
Uasin Gishu Governor Jonathan Bii welcomed the race to Eldoret and urged active runners to safeguard their legacies by investing in sustainable development projects.
